newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi businessmen propose domestic airline.
newsitem.headline: Saudi businessmen propose domestic airline.

text.p: Saudi Arabia is considering a private sector proposal to set up a domestic airline in a joint venture with the flag carrier Saudi Arabian Airlines Corp, officials were quoted as saying on Sunday.

Ismail Abu Dawood, chairman of the Jeddah Chamber of Commerce and Industry, said Saudi businessmen had recently informed the national airline they were interested in setting up the domestic company, Saudi newspapers reported.
"The new firm would be a joint venture between Saudi Arabian Airlines and Saudi businessmen and would purchase all the aircraft that Saudia wanted to sell," he said.

Abdullah al-Jehani, assistant director general for publicity and marketing at the airline, said the idea of the joint venture was well received at a recent meeting between Saudi businessmen and airline executives, the newspapers added.
"There is a comprehensive study on establishing such a company and on its economic feasibility," he said.
Saudi Arabian Airlines Corp is polishing up its image and restructuring its organisation to turn itself into an attractive commercial operation ahead of eventual privatisation.
The carrier, with 12.5 million passengers annually, is spending $6 billion on 61 new Boeing and McDonnell Douglas aircraft. Deliveries are due to start this month.
It has said it planned to sell some of its current 109-strong fleet when it receives the new planes.
The airline has vowed to turn losses it suffered for more than a decade, mainly due to subsidised fares, to profits.

Analysts say the carrier has the tricky task of getting a balance between providing reasonably-priced domestic airfares in the kingdom -- where cities are scattered over a 2.2 million square km (850,000 square miles) area -- with showing a profit.
Industry executives say up to 70 percent of the airline's operations are domestic and 30 percent international, but almost three-quarters of income is generated on international routes.
